items.caption: A modern redraw of 北 in an oracle-script style. The two forms appear turned away from each other, matching the proposed back-to-back conception; Shang-period examples are cited for this graph.
items.alt: Black oracle-style strokes form two human-like figures turned away from one another.
items.selection_reason: The visible paired figures support the graph’s proposed conception, and the cited study reports this form of the graph in Shang inscriptions. The image is a modern redraw, so it illustrates a script style rather than an excavated inscription.

items.caption: A modern redraw of 北 in the seal-script style associated with Shuowen Jiezi. The Han dictionary analyzes the graph as two people back-to-back, a conception the paleographic study says remains recognizable from Shang writing through the seal form.
items.alt: Black seal-style strokes form two tall figures facing away from each other.
items.selection_reason: This later dictionary-style form complements the oracle-style candidate and makes the reported continuity of the graphic conception visible without implying a detailed sequence of shape changes.

limitations.text: Both images are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not photographs or scans of ancient inscriptions. Their shapes illustrate the proposed back-to-back conception, but cannot independently establish the graph’s meaning or the history of the spoken word.

The proposed original sense related to turning against or having one’s back is not securely attested in the excavated examples surveyed by the study. 北 is reported as a loan graph for ‘north’ in Shang-period use; the semantic relationship between ‘back’ and ‘north’ remains a proposal.
